intent_en: To demonstrate that payroll taxes are capped, resulting in lower- and middle-income earners paying a larger portion of their income in taxes than the wealthiest individuals.
previous_intent: To demonstrate how the cap on payroll taxes creates a regressive burden, highlighting that lower and middle-income earners pay a significantly higher percentage of their income than the wealthiest individuals.
narration_support: That means the rich pay a really small portion of their income toward payroll taxes. And poor people in the middle class pay way more.
chart_support: Bar chart displaying the share of income paid as payroll taxes across income groups from poorest to richest, with the bars for the lower and middle classes being much higher than the near-zero bars for the richest individuals.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly describes the disparity in tax burden due to capping, and the chart visualizes this with high bars for the lower/middle income groups (highlighted by a red box) and near-zero bars for the richest group.
